name: @forguncy-react-workspace/dev-harness
//exports: `.` is the node half: the Vite plugin, the host-substitution plan, and provenance.
`./mount` is the browser half — the only module a page loads. The split is by *graph*, not
by tidiness: the generated entry imports `./mount` by package name, and routing that through
`.` would pull `node:module` into the page's graph. That is the same defect `core/browser`
exists to fix, and the harness must not reintroduce it one layer up.
//dependencies: `react` / `react-dom` are the harness's *host substitutions*, not an implementation detail.
They are pinned to the versions #5 measured on Forguncy 12.0.100 (19.2.7) because the dev
loop renders Cell source against the React the page will provide — a different version would
make local feedback evidence about a different target. They are dependencies rather than
devDependencies for the same reason: `hostModuleAliases()` resolves them from this package
at dev-server configuration time, so they have to be installed wherever the plugin runs.
Examples deliberately do *not* install them (`examples/host-antd/package.json` records why:
installing a `host`-decided package is a silent escape hatch for a broken interception), so
the harness supplying the substitution is what makes `vp dev` able to render a Cell at all.
`host-modules.ts` checks the installed version against #5's record and reports a mismatch
rather than trusting the pin.
`vite` is a dependency because the plugin's own public types describe Vite hooks it composes
(`DevHarnessVitePlugin`), and because a harness that resolves `optimizeDeps`/`resolve` settings
for a Vite server has to be able to name that server's version. The plugin is still typed
structurally, like `vite-plugin-fgc`'s, so nothing here *imports* Vite at runtime.
`@vitejs/plugin-react-swc` is a *runtime* dependency, not a devDependency, because the
harness plugin includes it in the Vite config it returns: React Fast Refresh is what makes
an edit to a Cell's source keep the component's state, and without it `vp dev` degrades to
a full page reload. It is loaded from this package's own tree, so a project does not have
to install it to get the loop #23 defines.
